note: Wikimedia Commons, “Felice Campi, Fresco Painting of Saint Mark the Evangelist (1809).jpg”; artist as recorded there: Felice Campi — fetched 03 October 2026 at 1200px. The licence is as Commons records it. Identified as this saint because: A Western fresco painting, not an icon, acceptable in a hero slot under the 3 October 2026 ruling. Commons describes it as Saint Mark the Evangelist with the lion, by Felice Campi, 1809 — the winged lion being the evangelist's own symbol, which separates him from Mark of Arethusa and the other Marks of the calendar. Commons describes it: Saint Mark the Evangelist with the lion, a triangular spandrel painting by Felice Campi (1809), executed as a companion to the central vault fresco *Coronation of the Madonna* in the Parish Church of Saint Mary of the Assumption.
